## Body

# Gates must cover queue re-entry and surviving work

An admission mutex around fresh sends and retirement is not the whole lifecycle boundary. Enumerate every transition into queued: a failed drain releases its delivering claim, and boot recovery requeues claims that delivery never admitted. An in-flight request plus an ended holding can otherwise evade a queued-only retirement check.

Pij store owned_write explicitly outlives request cancellation. Blocking community-writer jobs also outlive their async waiter. A gate owned only by that waiter can be dropped while its mutation continues. Move ownership with surviving work and test aborts after admission, not only ordinary concurrent ordering.

The PR 135 repair at 3ecec77 closes F002/F003 and preserves the per-role batch refusal. CI executes all three new regressions, but those cases do not cover in-flight requeue or cancelled-waiter ownership. These residual schedules are source counterexamples; no local reproduction was claimed.

Proof precision: the resume regression seeds the failed state and proves recovery; do not describe it as fault injection. The gate regression queues both operations behind a lock, but uses timed waits for their order; an entered-wait handshake would make its scheduling pressure causal.

magicWand: a reusable lifecycle scenario with explicit claim, persistence-admitted, caller-cancelled and commit-finished barriers.

difficulties: treating queued as the only admission state misses re-entry; keeping an async guard in a caller is not sufficient when the write is independently owned. Shared LOG updates need one generated append, never a read-modify-write or a serialization window.
